subject: Re: Hosted API latency & throughput drop - urgent (customer: Velocity AI)
body:
--- Message 1/7 ---
From: support@velocity.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:22:08 -0700
Subject: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Hi Jonas / Hannah,

We started seeing a sharp p95/p99 latency increase and a severe drop in token-per-second throughput on our Hosted API integration around 11:35 PDT today, right after the 11:30 deployment you mentioned in the release notes. Summary of what we see from our side:
- p95 latency: ~230ms -> 1.2s
- p99 latency: ~600ms -> 3.4s
- Token/sec throughput: ~1800 tps -> ~420 tps (for our short-sequence traffic)
- 5xx error rate: 0.1% -> 2.7%

Our customers are impacted for short chat-turns (<= 64 tokens). We captured sample request IDs and attached a small request dump and a few aggregated logs (filenames attached). Can you confirm whether anything changed in the kernel selection / quantization paths today? This started immediately after the deploy from your side, and is blocking traffic for several of our teams.

We need an urgent investigation and either a rollback window or a mitigation plan. Please advise ETA.

Regards,
Samira Patel
Ops Lead, Velocity AI

Attachments: velocity-sample-reqs-20270411.txt, screenshot-metrics.png

--- Message 2/7 ---
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: support@velocity.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:39:52 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Samira, thanks for the quick heads up and the samples — that helps. We're pulling traces now.

Immediate plan:
- Engineering (cc Marissa, Monica) will triage kernel/quant selector config and review the 11:30 deploy artifacts.
- We'll collect a short list of affected request IDs and return heatmaps & traces by EOD PDT.
- If we confirm a regression tied to the recent selector change we'll propose a rollback window and communicate impact.

Can you confirm a good maintenance window if we need to roll back? Also are you seeing this only for short sequence traffic? Your note suggests <=64 tokens — that's consistent with a selector edge case we've seen in internal tests.

I'll keep you posted every hour.

— Jonas
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3/7 ---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, support@velocity.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:05:13 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Folks — preliminary findings from the runtime team: we pushed a kernel-selector optimization at 11:28 that changes the selection policy for short vs long sequences. The intention was to prefer the new "fast-kernel-v2" for long sequences and a compatibility path for short sequences. Unfortunately, there's a quantization routing bug when the model is served under q8_0 quant profile where short-sequence requests are routed to a fallback path ("compat-kernel") with a significantly slower microkernel for the current GPU shader. The quantized compatibility kernel is ~3-4x slower for the short sequences in the observed hardware, explaining both the tps drop and the p95/p99 spikes.

Root cause hypothesis: an incorrect kernel-compatibility map in the selector config that wasn't covered by the short-sequence perf test.

Immediate mitigation we can do today:
- Option A (fast): Back out the kernel-selector change (config rollback) across the affected pool — low-risk, immediate improvement expected.
- Option B (medium): Apply a targeted hotfix to the selector to correct the q8_0 mapping — requires a short CI run (~45 min) and can be deployed to canary then prod.

I'll be ready to run the rollback at 18:00 PDT if Velocity approves. We'll monitor sampling traces and a small user bucket post-rollback and report metrics at +15m / +60m.

Apologies — we should have had a short-sequence perf gate in front of that change. Taking ownership to deliver the hotfix and postmortem.

— Marissa
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

--- Message 4/7 ---
From: ops@velocity.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:33:01 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Thanks — we can approve an immediate rollback now. The impact window is broad for us, so sooner is better. Please confirm expected user-visible changes and whether any in-flight requests will fail. Also confirm whether you will provide a credit given this regression.

We'd prefer no more than a single rollback attempt. If you can commit to 18:00 PDT and a brief verification plan, we'll hold traffic for that window.

— Samira (Velocity)

--- Message 5/7 ---
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:10:44 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Team — thank you for the quick triage. Please prepare an executive summary for Velocity and Ops that includes:
- Short timeline of events and root cause (one paragraph)
- The customer-facing remediation plan and rollback timing (we've tentatively proposed 18:00 PDT)
- Proposed goodwill gesture / credit (finance, cc Laura) — suggest starting with a bill credit of 10% of last 24h usage while we complete the postmortem.

Keep the material concise; we'll escalate to Sales leadership if the customer pushes harder.

— Rishi
Head of Commercial Operations

--- Message 6/7 ---
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: support@velocity.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 06:45:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + errors on Hosted API since April 11 deploy

Samira — following up from our end: we have the rollback scheduled for 18:00 PDT tonight. If that time still works, we'll proceed with a single rollback and do +15 / +60 minute checks. Laura is reviewing a provisional credit (Rishi proposed 10%) and will confirm before we finalize customer comms. Marissa will post live updates in this thread during the rollback.

Thank you for being flexible — we'll aim for no further disruptions.

— Hannah
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

--- Message 7/7 ---
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: support@velocity.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 19:03:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency & throughput drop - rollback complete

Samira — quick update and summary of outcome from the rollback we executed at 18:40 PDT:
- Action taken: rolled back kernel-selector config on the "hosted-prod-us-central" pool to the pre-11:28 policy.
- Immediate impact (aggregated across Velocity's production pool):
  * p95: 1.2s -> 280ms
  * p99: 3.4s -> 420ms
  * Token/sec throughput: 420 -> 1700 (short-sequence workload)
  * 5xx error rate: 2.7% -> 0.12%
- Attachments: system-aggregate logs and a short perf summary CSV attached (perf-summary-20270412.csv).

Next steps we will take internally:
1) Ship targeted selector-hotfix to correct the q8_0 routing; include an explicit short-sequence perf gate AND a canary rollout. Timeline: hotfix PR today, canary + prod patch tomorrow.
2) Postmortem and customer-facing one-pager within 48 hours.
3) Laura to confirm goodwill credit and finalize wording.

We regret the impact and appreciate Velocity's patience. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge to walk through the postmortem draft once it's ready.

— Jonas
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above: system-aggregate-20270411.log.gz, perf-summary-20270412.csv
